```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(smma)
```

**smma** helps answer *what is this receptor-model factor made of?* A PMF
factor is a statistical pattern. SMMA (Source Mixture Matching Analysis)
fits it as a non-negative mixture of independently measured source
profiles and tells you how stable that answer is.

The package works with any analytes and any source library. The
examples use polycyclic aromatic compounds (PACs) and petroleum
biomarkers in coastal sediments.

## 1. Your inputs

You need four tables. CSV or Excel both work.

| Input | Shape | Reader |
|---|---|---|
| Factor profiles | species x factors (EPA PMF "Profiles_conc"), or factors x species | `read_factor_profiles()` |
| Factor contributions | samples x factors | `read_factor_contributions()` |
| Source library | one row per source profile: `source`, `category`, analyte columns | `read_source_library()` |
| Optional: S/N per factor, Kow per analyte | factors x analytes; one value per analyte | `read_sn()`, `read_kow()` |

Analyte columns must use the **same names** in all tables. Missing values
in the library are allowed. They are treated as zero in the fit (see
`fill_library_gaps()` and `update_library()` to test that assumption).

The example data are the four-factor PMF solution for 211 intertidal
sediments from British Columbia and a 371-profile library:

```{r}
ex <- smma_example()
ex$profiles[, 1:6]
head(ex$library[, 1:5])
```

## 2. Prepare and fit

```{r}
inp <- smma_prepare(ex$profiles, ex$library)
inp
```

`smma_prepare()` keeps the analytes shared by factors and library and
normalizes every profile to unit sum. A quick point estimate:

```{r}
fit <- smma_fit(inp, kow = ex$kow, sn = ex$sn)
head(fit[order(fit$factor, -fit$weight), ], 8)
```

## 3. Bootstrap for uncertainty

`smma_bootstrap()` resamples analytes with replacement, refits, and
weights draws by fit quality. Use `B = 1000` or more for real work. A
small `B` keeps this vignette fast.

```{r}
bt <- smma_bootstrap(inp, B = 100, seed = 42, kow = ex$kow, sn = ex$sn)
bt
mix <- smma_best_mixture(bt)
mix$categories
```

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
plot_smma(bt, min_weight = 0.02)
```

**Weights.** Each analyte's weight is the product of a Kow term (particle
affinity) and the factor's S/N. If your Kow table holds log10 Kow (the
usual tabulated form), keep the default `kow_args = list(input_scale = "log10")`.
For dissolved-phase samples, use `kow_args = list(matrix = "water")`.

## 4. Back to samples

`attribute_sources()` converts the factor mixtures into source-resolved
concentrations for any grouping of analytes. Here the groupings are
EPA16, parent, alkylated and total PACs:

```{r}
groups <- analyte_groupings(names(ex$profiles))
att <- attribute_sources(ex$contributions, ex$profiles, mix$sources, groups)
head(att)
```

Summarise by any sample grouping (here by sampling campaign, read from
the sample code):

```{r}
camp <- data.frame(sample = unique(att$sample))
camp$campaign <- sub("_.*", "", camp$sample)
s <- summarise_attribution(att[att$grouping == "EPA16", ], groups = camp,
                           group_col = "campaign", B = 200, seed = 1)
head(s[order(s$group, -s$mean), c("group", "category", "n", "mean", "lo", "hi", "share_pct")])
```

To regroup sources into your own categories without refitting, pass a
`category_map` data frame (`source`, `category`) to `attribute_sources()`.

## 5. Other lines of evidence

```{r}
diagnostic_ratios(ex$profiles)
head(alkylation_indices(ex$profiles))
d <- profile_distances(ex$profiles, ex$library)
best_matches(d)[1:6, ]
```

## 6. Check what the library can resolve

Simulate factors from known mixtures and see whether SMMA recovers them.
This is a good first step with a new library:

```{r}
fo <- ex$library$source[ex$library$category == "Fuel oil (fresh)"][1]
bb <- ex$library$source[ex$library$category == "Biomass combustion"][1]
sim <- smma_simulate(ex$library, list(test = setNames(c(0.6, 0.4), c(fo, bb))),
                     noise_sd = 0.1, seed = 1)
r <- smma_fit(smma_prepare(sim, ex$library))
head(r[order(-r$weight), c("source", "category", "weight")], 5)
```

## 7. Using your own naming scheme

Analyte groupings, diagnostic ratios and alkylation indices read column
names from an *analyte scheme*. Start from `default_analyte_scheme()` and edit
it for your columns, for example:

```{r}
sch <- default_analyte_scheme()
sch$ratio["phe"]          # which column is phenanthrene
names(sch$homologues)
```

## 8. Spatial tools

`classify_sites()` labels sites Urban/Mixed/Remote from distances to
population centres (`default_population_tiers()` sets the radii).
`distance_to_features()` (needs **sf**) and `fit_distance_decay()` (needs
**nlme**) test whether factor contributions decline with distance from
infrastructure layers. See `analysis/R/03_spatial_regression.R` in the
repository for a complete example.
